headline: Salman Shah murder case: Accused 'Don' arrested at airport
summary: Mohammad Ashraful Haque, known as Don, was detained by immigration police while attempting to fly to Saudi Arabia for Umrah.
details: Immigration police arrested Mohammad Ashraful Haque, widely known as Don, at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka yesterday.
The arrest occurred as the accused was attempting to leave the country for Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah.
Following the arrest, he was handed over to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) for further legal proceedings.
The CID Dhaka Metropolitan West unit stated that the case was filed with Ramna Police Station.
Airport authorities had been alerted to stop any accused named in the FIR from leaving the country, following a court directive.
Salman Shah, the iconic actor, was found dead at his Eskaton Road residence on September 6, 1996, at the age of 25.
caption:
A major breakthrough in a 28-year-old cold case. Accused 'Don' arrested while trying to flee the country.

Immigration police arrested Mohammad Ashraful Haque, widely known as Don, at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka yesterday.

The arrest occurred as the accused was attempting to leave the country for Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah.

Following the arrest, he was handed over to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) for further legal proceedings.

The CID Dhaka Metropolitan West unit stated that the case was filed with Ramna Police Station.

Airport authorities had been alerted to stop any accused named in the FIR from leaving the country, following a court directive.

Salman Shah, the iconic actor, was found dead at his Eskaton Road residence on September 6, 1996, at the age of 25.

headline_marked: 10 Bangladeshis [[killed in sofa factory fire]] in Saudi Arabia
headline: 10 Bangladeshis killed in sofa factory fire in Saudi Arabia
summary: All the victims were residents of Naogaon's Atrai Upazila. The Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment has confirmed the incident.
details: A devastating fire broke out at a sofa manufacturing factory in the Manfuah area of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Sunday afternoon, resulting in the deaths of 10 Bangladeshi workers.

The victims are all from the Atrai Upazila of Naogaon district. The news was confirmed by the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment and the Deputy Commissioner of Naogaon, Mohammad Saiful Islam.
The deceased include Sagar (31), Majidul (34), Farid Sheikh (32), Sumon (35), Hasibul Hasan (27), Mohun Pramanik (42), Sumon Pramanik, Rubel Hossain (30), Koli Pramanik (35), and Abdul Jalil (38).

Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury expressed deep grief over the loss, describing the deaths as heartbreaking and acknowledging the workers' immense contribution to the national economy.
The Bangladesh Embassy in Saudi Arabia is maintaining constant communication with local authorities and the site of the accident to facilitate the process.
The government has issued instructions to ensure the quick repatriation of the bodies and to provide necessary government assistance and compensation to the bereaved families.
caption:
10 Bangladeshi workers from Naogaon have died in a horrific factory fire in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

A devastating fire broke out at a sofa manufacturing factory in the Manfuah area of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Sunday afternoon, resulting in the deaths of 10 Bangladeshi workers.

The victims are all from the Atrai Upazila of Naogaon district. The news was confirmed by the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment and the Deputy Commissioner of Naogaon, Mohammad Saiful Islam.

The deceased include Sagar (31), Majidul (34), Farid Sheikh (32), Sumon (35), Hasibul Hasan (27), Mohun Pramanik (42), Sumon Pramanik, Rubel Hossain (30), Koli Pramanik (35), and Abdul Jalil (38).

Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury expressed deep grief over the loss, describing the deaths as heartbreaking and acknowledging the workers' immense contribution to the national economy.

The Bangladesh Embassy in Saudi Arabia is maintaining constant communication with local authorities and the site of the accident to facilitate the process.

The government has issued instructions to ensure the quick repatriation of the bodies and to provide necessary government assistance and compensation to the bereaved families.
